role.altitude: The criminal justice teacher keeps choosing books and readings, talking with students and colleagues, judging students for letters and deciding in committees; checking availability, mailing lists to several desks, copying grades into notes, merging mailed comments and formatting bibliographies shrink.
reach: Committee members and programmes receiving letters
skills_to_grow: Maintaining reading lists in the library system
Rewriting drafted letters in their own judgement
role.ambitious_version: A teacher whose reading lists and letters take less clerical time and more thought.

tasks.short: Review textbook options, discuss with colleagues, request desk copies, check availability and licences, send choices to bookstore and library, enter the reading list in the course page and check library copies to select and obtain materials such as textbooks.

steps.what: Teacher reviews textbook options and sample copies
Teacher discusses the choice of materials with colleagues
Teacher requests desk copies from publishers by mail
Teacher asks the library by mail about holdings and digital licences
Teacher enters the textbook choices: sent separately to the bookstore and library today, built once in the library's reading list tool after the change
Teacher checks the final reading list: titles, editions, numbers and access notes are right
Teacher releases the checked list from the reading list tool to the bookstore, the library and the course page
Teacher puts the reading list on the course page: typing it today, checking the published list after the change
Teacher checks the copies in the library

tasks.design: The teacher builds the course reading list once in the library's reading list tool. It shows holdings and digital licences for each title; the teacher checks the list and releases it once to the bookstore, the library and the course page. This replaces asking the library by mail, mailing each desk and retyping the list. Reviewing options, discussing with colleagues, requesting desk copies and checking copies stay with the teacher.

approvals.approved_version: The reading list with titles, editions and numbers exactly as checked by the teacher in s5b, released once from the reading list tool to the bookstore, the library and the course page; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: The same list was mailed to several desks and retyped in the course page.
tasks.enabler_now: Reading list tools linked to the catalogue, bookstore and learning environment.
tasks.still_hard: Materials not held by any library.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a text that fits both police practice and theory.

reach.learn: Whether lists arrive in time to buy copies.

evidence.claim: A reference manager and the library catalogue handle reading lists; every title must resolve in the catalogue.

assumptions: Boundary: selecting and obtaining materials; compiling bibliographies for outside reading (task 6209) is in this set and preparing course materials (task 6198) is a sibling task.
s4, s5 and s6 save mail rounds and retyping of the same list; checking and releasing the list keep their full time.
Reviewing, discussing, desk copies and checking keep their full time.
research_questions: Are textbooks available at course start more often?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the tool is not linked to the bookstore, so choices are still mailed and s5 keeps 80 (7.5); high: tool linked as assumed (8.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Receive the student's request, collect grades and notes, talk with the student, write letters of recommendation for students, check and sign them, answer follow-ups and upload them to each programme.

steps.what: Student requests the letter and gives CV, programme and deadline
Teacher copies the student's grades and projects into notes for the letter
Teacher talks with the student about goals
Teacher writes letters of recommendation for students

loop.input: The student's grades and projects from the records, the teacher's notes and the target programme.
loop.output: A draft letter in the teacher's structure.
loop.check: Every fact must trace to the records or the teacher's notes; the teacher checks that each fact says what the record says and rewrites the judgement of the student in their own words.
loop.stop: The teacher writes the letter when two drafts read generic.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each letter argues for one student and one destination.

steps.what: Teacher checks the final letter: every statement is true of this student and fits the programme, and signs it
Teacher uploads the letter to each programme's portal
Teacher answers the student's follow-ups and deadline reminders

approvals.approved_version: The letter text exactly as checked and signed by the teacher in s5, uploaded once to each programme portal the student named; any change needs a new check and signature.

tasks.design: With the student's request, the student's grades and projects are pulled from the learning environment and grade records into one sheet, instead of the teacher copying them. A drafting step writes a first letter from that sheet, the teacher's notes and the target programme. The teacher rewrites the judgement in their own words, signs and uploads it. Talking with the student, follow-ups and uploads stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts were copied from records and every letter written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Record exports and drafting tied to the teacher's notes.
tasks.still_hard: Students the teacher knows only from one large class.
tasks.human_edge: Vouching for a student's integrity for police work.
tasks.altitude: Less drafting from scratch; the endorsement stays.

evidence.claim: Recommendation letters suit a generator from records where a model drafts and the teacher signs.
A grade or admission judgement set solely by a model is likely an article 22 decision; here the teacher writes and signs the judgement.

assumptions: Boundary: writing recommendation letters; advising students on careers (task 6204) is a sibling task.
Student records are used only at the student's request.
s4 is priced at 70 because the teacher rewrites every judgement.
Students' request time is shown in s1 and does not change.
Talking, signing, follow-ups and uploads keep their full time.
research_questions: Do letters arrive earlier before deadlines?

incremental.description: Teacher keeps short notes on students for later letters.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most drafts need rewriting beyond the judgement, so s4 keeps 85 (13.2); high: drafts usable after rewriting the judgement as assumed (20.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read committee papers, attend meetings, draft committee documents, take minutes in turn, comment on drafts, follow own actions and discuss issues to serve on academic or administrative committees.

steps.what: Teacher reads committee papers on institutional policies and academic issues
Teacher attends committee meetings
Teacher drafts committee documents such as policy changes
Teacher takes and types minutes in the short template when it is their turn
Teacher checks the final minutes and action items: each decision and action, owner and date says what was agreed
Teacher puts the checked action items on the shared action list, which reminds owners
Teacher comments on drafts and answers committee mail
Teacher keeps track of own committee actions in the mailbox
Teacher discusses committee issues with colleagues

tasks.design: Committee drafts live in one shared document with tracked changes against the current policy, so members comment there instead of mailing versions. Minutes use a short template; the minute taker checks the action items, with owner and date, and puts them once on a shared action list with reminders, so nobody tracks actions in a mailbox. Reading papers, meetings, drafting and discussions stay with the teacher.

approvals.approved_version: The minutes' action items with owners and dates exactly as checked by the teacher in s4b, put once on the shared action list that sends reminders; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Drafts and actions travelled by mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared documents with tracked changes and action lists with reminders.
tasks.still_hard: Committees spanning institutions with separate systems.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the compromise a divided committee will accept.

evidence.claim: Shared documents and action lists replace mailed versions and mailbox tracking.

assumptions: Boundary: serving on committees; department administration (task 6212) is a sibling task.
s5 saves merging mailed versions; s6 saves tracking actions by hand. s4 keeps 85 because the template gives only the layout; checking and publishing action items keep their full time.
Reading, meetings and discussions keep their full time.
research_questions: Do committee actions close on time more often?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: members keep mailing versions, so s5 keeps 90 (5.2); high: drafts in one shared document as assumed (7.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search catalogues and databases, select readings, check availability, format citations, keep the course reading list, discuss with librarians and publish the list to compile bibliographies of specialized materials for outside reading assignments.

steps.what: Teacher searches catalogues and databases for specialized materials

loop.input: The course topics and an abstract and citation database plus the library catalogue.
loop.output: Suggested titles with short summaries, each with DOI or catalogue record.
loop.check: Every suggestion must resolve by DOI or in the catalogue, else it is dropped; the teacher checks each summary against the abstract and keeps only titles that fit the course topic.
loop.stop: The teacher searches by hand when known key works are missing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Criminal justice literature spans law, sociology and policing journals.

steps.what: Teacher reads abstracts and selects the readings
Teacher checks library availability and access for each item
Teacher formats the bibliographies in the citation style
Teacher keeps a separate spreadsheet of readings per course
Teacher discusses readings with colleagues or librarians
Teacher checks the final reading list: citations match the readings and access links work
Teacher publishes the checked reading list to students: by mail today, from the reading list tool to the course page after the change

tasks.design: A literature tool suggests titles with summaries. Every suggestion must resolve by DOI or in the library catalogue, otherwise it is dropped, and the teacher reads abstracts and selects. The library's reading list tool checks availability and access through the catalogue, formats citations in the chosen style, holds the list per course instead of a separate spreadsheet, and the teacher checks it and publishes it once to the course page. Selecting readings and discussing them stay with the teacher.

approvals.approved_version: The reading list with citations and access links exactly as checked by the teacher in s6b, published once to the course page; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Titles were searched, checked and formatted by hand and kept in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Literature tools with linked sources and library reading list tools.
tasks.still_hard: Grey literature such as police reports and court documents.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing readings that challenge students' views of policing.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and formatting; selection stays.

evidence.claim: A literature database tool gives topic summaries and foundational papers, for compiling bibliographies.
Invented references pass plagiarism checks unflagged, so every suggestion must resolve.

assumptions: Boundary: compiling bibliographies; selecting textbooks (task 6203) is in this set and keeping abreast of the field (task 6194) is a sibling task.
s3, s4 and s5 save checking, formatting and keeping the list twice.
Input contract for s3: about 80% of items are held in the catalogue or licensed databases; s3 is priced at that share.
Selecting and discussing keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of reading lists per year.
research_questions: Do broken or missing reading links fall?

incremental.description: Teacher adds grey literature by hand.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of the items are in the catalogue or licensed databases, so s3 keeps 60 and s4 keeps 50 (21.9); high: about 80% covered as assumed (26.3).
